target: this repository, checked out at target_ref into a throwaway worktree
notes: Natural questions a person asks about a repository they do not know. They deliberately do not all ask for a diagram, and each targets a different level, so the set discriminates on level selection: the skill's central judgement. Structural answers must take their diagram from vizzle (the `%% vizzle:` trailer is the evidence); behavioural answers are drawn by hand; the trivial question gets no diagram. Rewritten from code-comprehension's comprehend-code evals, whose assertions required hand-drawn C4 (docs/plans/impl/skill-set.md D5).

evals.name: repo-shape
evals.prompt: I've just been handed this repository and I have no idea how the pieces fit together. What are the moving parts, and how do they depend on each other?
evals.expected_level: the repo's components, from vizzle component
evals.expected_output: A component diagram taken from `vizzle component` (the Rust core, the PyO3 bindings, the Python CLI, the site and web packages), then a walkthrough anchored to real paths, then where to look next.

evals.name: doc-check-sequence
evals.prompt: When CI runs `vizzle doc --dir docs/diagrams --check`, what actually happens, in order? I want to know where it decides a document is stale and what makes it exit non-zero.
evals.expected_level: behaviour: a sequence diagram, drawn by hand
evals.expected_output: A sequenceDiagram from the CLI's doc command through managed.py (discover, read, scope_of) into the Rust core (curated_diagram_from_dir or class_diagram_from_dir) and back, with the stale comparison and the non-zero exit anchored to cli.py. A component diagram here is a level-selection failure.

needles.managed: managed.py, which finds and reads the documents
needles.curated: the curated render in the core

evals.name: curated-zoom
evals.prompt: I want to add a new manifest `kind` to the curated diagrams that `vizzle doc` renders. Before I touch anything, explain how that part of vizzle-core is put together and where a new kind would have to be handled.
evals.expected_level: one module's structure and flow: a class diagram from vizzle, or a hand-drawn flowchart labelled as such
evals.expected_output: A diagram of how curated diagrams are produced (manifest → CLI → bindings → curated::render), either from `vizzle class` or drawn by hand and said to be, with the walkthrough naming where kinds are handled: is_curated_only, stereotype and members_for, anchored to curated.rs. curated.rs holds only two types (Entry, Manifest), so a derived class diagram alone cannot carry the answer; the grader does not require derivation here.

needles.is_curated_only: where the curated-only kinds are listed
needles.stereotype: where each kind gets its stereotype line

evals.name: restraint-one-function
evals.prompt: quick one: in crates/vizzle-core/src/curated.rs, what does is_curated_only return true for, and why does it matter?
evals.expected_output: A short prose answer naming the two kinds (const and external) and the consequence (no source is read, so a missing symbol is not an error), with a path:line anchor. A diagram, or padding into the four-part brief, is the failure.
